style_explainers.Blanco: Unaged, or rested less than two months.
style_explainers.Rosa Blanco: Blanco briefly rested in red-wine barrels, which tints it pink.
style_explainers.Reposado: Rested in oak for 2 to 12 months.
style_explainers.Añejo: Aged in oak for 1 to 3 years.
style_explainers.Extra Añejo: Aged in oak for at least 3 years.
style_explainers.Joven & Gold: Joven blends unaged and aged tequila; gold tequilas may also be colored.
style_explainers.Infused: Tequila infused with fruit or botanicals.
style_explainers.Mezcal: Agave spirit, usually pit-roasted, which gives it a smoky taste.
style_explainers.Sotol: Made from the desert spoon plant (sotol), not agave.
style_explainers.Bourbon: American whiskey made mostly from corn and aged in new charred oak.
style_explainers.Tennessee: Like bourbon, but filtered through maple charcoal before aging.
style_explainers.Canadian: Canadian whisky, usually a smooth blend of grains.
style_explainers.Rye: Whiskey made mostly from rye grain; spicier than bourbon.
style_explainers.Blended: A blend of malt and grain whiskies from Scotland.
style_explainers.Single Malt: Malted-barley whisky from a single Scottish distillery.
style_explainers.London Dry: Juniper-forward gin that gets all its flavor in the still. It's a style, not a place.
style_explainers.Dark: Rum with deeper color and flavor.
